# Lab 6.9: Advanced Runtime, History-Based Optimisation & Short Query Mode

## What We Are Going to Do
Check which built-in optimisations are on, run a repeated query to see history-based optimisation, and run a small query in short query (job-optional) mode.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Check project options.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT option_name, option_value
FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.PROJECT_OPTIONS;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The advanced runtime and history-based optimisations are on by default. Settings appear here only if someone changed them.

2. **[SQL] Run the same heavy query three times.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT company, payment_type, APPROX_QUANTILES(fare, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_fare
FROM lab06.trips_flat
WHERE trip_miles &gt; 2
GROUP BY company, payment_type;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Turn off the cache first (**Query settings → Use cached results**).

3. **[CLI] See if history-based optimisations were applied.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT job_id, total_slot_ms, query_info.optimization_details
 FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_USER
 WHERE query LIKE "%median_fare%" AND creation_time &gt; TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
 ORDER BY creation_time'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Later runs can show optimisation details and lower slot time.

4. **[CLI] Run a short query without creating a job.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">pip install --quiet --upgrade google-cloud-bigquery
python3 - &lt;&lt;'EOF'
from google.cloud import bigquery
client = bigquery.Client(default_job_creation_mode="JOB_CREATION_OPTIONAL")
rows = client.query_and_wait("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.shakespeare`")
print(list(rows), "| job created:", rows.job_id is not None, "| query id:", rows.query_id)
EOF</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   For small queries, BigQuery may skip job creation and return faster. A `query_id` is still recorded.

5. **[Console] Use the same mode in the UI.** In **Query settings**, look for the **job creation** / short query option and turn it on for interactive exploration.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Advanced runtime | On by default |
| History-based optimisation | Learns from repeated queries |
| Short query mode | Small queries can run without a job |
| Proof | `optimization_details` and `query_id` |
